Topic 2.6: Symbolic

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello learner! Today we will learn about Symbolic. Read carefully, study the examples, do the practice, then try the revision quiz.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. write number symbols 1-20 on a surface for enjoyment
2. form number symbols 1-20 using ICT for digital literacy e) appreciate the use of numbers within their environment.

SECTION 3: LEARN STEP BY STEP

1. write number symbols 1-20 on a surface for enjoyment
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to write number symbols 1-20 on a surface for enjoyment. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

2. form number symbols 1-20 using ICT for digital literacy e) appreciate the use of numbers within their environment.
   In this part of the lesson, you learn to form number symbols 1-20 using ICT for digital literacy e) appreciate the use of numbers within their environment. Think about how you can do this at school and at home in Kenya.

SECTION 4: EXAMPLES

Example 1: At the market in your county, count 10 mangoes. Put them in 2 groups of 5. That is sorting and grouping.

Example 2: In class, count the desks in your row. Write the number in figures and in words.

Example 3: If you have 7 shillings and your parent gives you 5 more, you have 12 shillings. That is addition.

SECTION 5: TRY THIS

1. Read the examples above again. Underline two new words or ideas about Symbolic.
2. Explain Symbolic to a parent or classmate using your own words and one Kenyan example.
3. Draw or write three things that show you understand Symbolic.
4. Show that you can: write number symbols 1-20 on a surface for enjoyment
5. Complete the Work to do section, then attempt the Revision Quiz. Check Answers only after you finish.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (PRACTICE & REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Symbolic. Use examples from your school, home, or market.
2. Answer this question in your exercise book: Why is Symbolic important to you?
3. Make a short oral presentation (about one minute) to your parent or teacher.
4. List three ways you will practise this topic this week.

SECTION 8: REMEMBER

1. write number symbols 1-20 on a surface for enjoyment
2. form number symbols 1-20 using ICT for digital literacy e) appreciate the use of numbers within their environment.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open the Answers tab only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Learner lesson
